description: A platform-independent file lock for Python.

latest_release.body: ### Features - On Windows, `release_with_timeout` limits the caller's wait for release. If it raises `ReleasePendingError`, call `wait` on the exception from any thread for the result. On POSIX, release is synchronous ([#1107](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1107)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1100](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1100)) ### Bug fixes - `lock_descriptor` raises `TypeError` unless `blocking` is a `bool` ([#969](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/969)) by @feiiiiii5 and @gaborbernat. - On POSIX filesystems with atomic exchange, `SoftFileLock` restores a live marker after an interrupted exchange and removes its own unfinished marker during cleanup ([#1080](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1080)) by @gaborbernat. ([#993](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/993)) - Unix soft fallback markers exclude group and other writes even on filesystems without atomic exchange ([#1057](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1057)) by @gaborbernat. ([#994](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/994)) - `SoftFileLock`, `MarkerSoftFileLock` and `SoftFileLease` remove empty markers after a signal interrupts marker creation or stale-marker replacement ([#1049](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1049)) by @gaborbernat. ([#996](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/996)) - Unix locks select the soft fallback per resolved path, including after a directory change. The lock keeps its Unix type and supports `pid`, `is_lock_held_by_us`, `break_lock()` and `lifetime` during fallback ([#1057](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1057)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1000](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1000)) - On POSIX, `ReadWriteLock` and `AsyncReadWriteLock` raise `RuntimeError` in detected subinterpreters, including `InterpreterPoolExecutor` workers and mod_wsgi or uWSGI subinterpreters. Use the main interpreter or a separate process. Detection on embedded CPython 3.11 requires `_xxsubinterpreters` or `ctypes` access to the interpreter C API ([#1106](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1106)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1003](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1003)) - On Windows, `SoftFileLock` treats a symlink as an occupied marker and leaves its target untouched ([#1049](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1049)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1009](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1009)) - `SoftFileLock` and `SoftFileLease` clean up markers and descriptors across interrupted acquires and releases. POSIX unlink errors propagate, with a retry after close on filesystems that require it. Retry `release` if a timeout interrupts restoration of a displaced marker ([#1062](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1062)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1014](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1014)) - A singleton shared by relative and absolute paths refuses acquisition if a directory change redirects its stored lock path ([#1098](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1098)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1018](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1018)) - `ReadWriteLock` raises `RuntimeError` if a directory change redirects a singleton's cached database path ([#1058](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1058)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1019](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1019)) - `SoftFileLock`, `MarkerSoftFileLock` and `SoftFileLease` remove their pending recovery marker even if another process replaces the break name during rollback ([#1082](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1082)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1025](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1025)) - Single-threaded SQLite read and write lock waits allow Python signal handlers to run. Waiting writers keep their place ahead of new readers ([#1105](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1105)) by @gaborbernat. ([#1027](https://github.com/tox-dev/filelock/pull/1027)) - On POSIX, `SoftFileLock` tries to leave a one-byte recovery record if a full filesystem
